reference_semantics: direct_dependencies are author-declared logical premises. inherited_mechanisms record reused constructions or contextual authorities, including arguments proved again in full. scope: Twelve numbered additions consolidate inherited support theory, extend compact model-family synthesis, prove same-memory regularization and uniform-all-M stability, and give exact boundary examples. This is not twelve novelty claims.

statements.conclusion: A uniform initial row followed by pure alternating rows costs 34/11, below the one-row robust value 10/3. Every report-only deterministic routing of that same palette costs at least 10/3. The known-model qubit lift has the same all-initial-state values.

statements.claim_class: Principal new resource-preserving construction: no additional label, no physical reset, uniform over a fixed hidden model. It is distinct from inherited finite-prefix completion with growing memory.
classical_ingredients: Finite-dimensional positive-map order and compactness

statements.conclusion: The same command rows and M labels have initial cost <=U=b/(1-epsilon*b/c_*) and cost <=K=c^*/epsilon+U from every physical state at every label. Full-space exact cost witnesses obey these bounds.
hypotheses: Finite Hilbert dimension, finite command/report alphabets and arbitrary CP failure branches continuous in a compact fixed-model family.

internal_load_bearing_facts: Finiteness proved from finite restart generations; no circular inequality with an infinite expected cost.

statements.label: thm:r79-label-restart
statements.limits: Requires the all-initial-state cost guarantee. The hidden model never changes during execution; command rows remain identical but update probabilities change. The constants are upper bounds without sharpness claim.
statements.proof: Cut each label-1 segment at success or its first restart coin. Its cost is <=b and restart probability <=epsilon*b/c_*. Bound finite numbers of segments by a geometric sum, then use monotone convergence. From any label the first segment costs <=c^*/epsilon; after a restart the label-1 bound applies. Positive-cost transience gives full-space cost operators.

statements.claim_class: A quantitative refinement in a stronger structural class, using the classical resolvent perturbation mechanism; no claim that this classical mechanism is novel or the general square-root exponent is sharp.

statements.conclusion: All M simultaneously satisfy |V_M(U)-V_M(V)|<=zeta/kappa+c^* eta/kappa^2 without small-error restriction; the same holds for V_hist. Counted history completion has error at most C0(1-kappa)^T. Scalar geometric waiting proves local sharpness of both coefficients for 0<kappa<1.
hypotheses: Same finite-dimensional primitive interface and positive-cost conventions, with common cost ceiling c^*.
For every command and model in both compared compact families, success effect B_a>=kappa I with fixed 0<kappa<=1.

statements.label: cor:r79-positive-success
statements.limits: Uniform per-command success is stronger than common-dark-space exclusion. Exponential approximation is in history horizon, generally a power law in the number of history labels. Coefficient sharpness is local and does not classify support-degenerate instruments.
statements.proof: Bound every full-space inverse by 1/kappa and every positive cost witness by c^*/kappa. Subtract the two fixed-controller cost equations, apply the centered estimate, then take model suprema and controller infima. statements.conclusion: Exactly V1=2, V2=(1+sqrt(5))/2, and V_M=3/2 for M>=3, which also equals the unrestricted visible-history optimum. The two-label optimizer has model-specific supports (1,0) and (1,1).

internal_load_bearing_facts: In model 0 label 2 is inaccessible and dark; forcing a full-space potential produces the impossible inequality W_2>=1+W_2.
statements.label: prop:r79-golden-ratio-memory
statements.limits: A free mixed initializer changes the resource problem and attains 3/2 with two labels. The zero-success degeneracy is explicit; the separate positive example tests a different structural boundary.
statements.proof: One label minimizes max(1/r,1/(1-r)). For two label rows r,s, split r>=s and r<=s; maximal conditional success gives reciprocal bounds, while failure of the first call gives affine bounds. Balancing max(1/r,1+r) gives the golden ratio, attained by the explicit transition rule. Any first command incurs worst cost at least 3/2; three labels attain it.
